instruction: My roommates and I share amazon prime, which I just paid for yesterday. Request the money for it from them on venmo assuming equal share among all, with a description note, "Amazon Prime Subscription". Skip the one/s who have already paid me for it.
notes: Apps: amazon (prime subscription price paid yesterday), phone (roommate contacts via relationship filter), venmo (check received transactions, send requests). Knowledge gating: create_payment_request requires prime-cost-known (amazon.show_prime_subscriptions), roommates-known (phone.search_contacts), and payments-checked (venmo.show_transactions with query 'prime'; agent inspects which roommates already sent money for it). The problem encodes a representative scenario of 3 roommates with roommate-3 having already paid (static already-paid fact, which blocks a request to them); the real set of unpaid roommates is determined at runtime from venmo.show_transactions, and the number of roommates/unpaid roommates in the problem (and the arity of supervisor-complete-task) should be adjusted if the environment differs. contact-email is a static database mapping; roommates-known is the knowledge flag set by the single search_contacts call (avoids quantified effects). Share amount = prime price / (roommates + supervisor), equal split; description must be exactly 'Amazon Prime Subscription'. Each unpaid roommate gets exactly one request (not (request-sent ?p) guard). supervisor-complete-task takes the two unpaid roommates as record parameters (not API args) so its precondition is the lifted conjunction of the goal; no answer is passed since the task is not a question.
